title: Not an MCP server — no MCP protocol, transport, or tool registration
evidence: go.mod (module brazilian-soccer-mcp) declares ZERO dependencies — no MCP SDK. main.go:425 Run() logs the 10 tool names and returns nil at main.go:451 (the 'Start HTTP server' comment is a no-op). main.go:466 main() then blocks on `select {}` serving nothing. The 10 Handle* methods (main.go:42-422) match an MCP tool-handler shape but are never wired to any JSON-RPC/stdio transport nor registered — grep for mcp|jsonrpc|stdio|register|ListenAndServe finds only the struct comment and the log line. CONFIRMED: second opinion agrees with the first evaluator.
suggestion: Add an MCP SDK (or stdio JSON-RPC loop), register the 10 Handle* methods as tools, and have Run() actually serve requests.

title: Test gate fails: 30 of 32 tests fail on a hardcoded relative data path
evidence: test_coverage=0.045 in retort.db/scores.json. All 32 tests load data via NewDataLoader("data/kaggle") (data/loader_test.go:9, query/handler_test.go:11 and 17 more). `go test ./...` sets CWD to each package dir, so the relative path resolves to data/data/kaggle and query/data/kaggle — neither exists; the CSVs live at module-root data/kaggle (confirmed: 6 CSVs present there). LoadAll() then errors and t.Fatalf fires. Only the 2 pure-function tests that never load data pass (TestLoader_normalizeTeamName, TestLoader_parseBrazilianDate). _agent_stdout.log shows the agent diagnosing this exact path issue as the run ended. CONFIRMED.
suggestion: Resolve the data dir relative to the module root (e.g. runtime.Caller or a DATA_DIR env fallback, or t.Chdir to module root), or pass an absolute test path.

title: Comprehensive test suite exists but does not execute (query capabilities untested at runtime)
evidence: 32 well-structured test functions across data/loader_test.go (14) and query/handler_test.go (18) exercise loading, match/team/player queries, standings and H2H — but 30 fail to run due to the hardcoded relative data path (see test-gate). how_to_verify requires 'tests execute (test_coverage > 0)'; effective coverage is 0.045, so the capabilities are essentially unverified. No t.Skip usages (0 skips).
suggestion: Fix the data-path resolution so the suite runs; the assertions themselves look sound.

title: Head-to-head goals-for tally miscounts when the queried team plays away
evidence: query/handler.go GetTeamHeadToHead (line 154) — flagged by summary/index.md; team1 goals are attributed from the home_goal column without swapping when team1 is the away side, undercounting Team1GoalsFor. Untested at runtime because the H2H tests are among the 30 that fail to execute.
suggestion: Attribute goals by comparing the normalized team name to home_team/away_team per match rather than assuming home.

title: Match filtering supports season but not an explicit date range
evidence: query/handler.go MatchQuery (line 24) exposes Season and a single DateTime field; SearchMatches (line 68) filters on exact Season only — no from/to date-range filter. R4 asks for 'date range and/or season'; the season half is met (implemented).
suggestion: Add StartDate/EndDate to MatchQuery and range-filter on the parsed match date.
